- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., > +2.0% from prior 10d avg), model often overshoots — reduce forecast 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- In low-sentiment periods, model frequently overpredicts mean reversion — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to align with persistent trend.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show rising sentiment (e.g., > 0.1), model often lags — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture momentum.
- For 30d horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action — apply +0.5–1.5% bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overforecast — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overconfidence bias.
